notes: Recorded here because refusing an instruction is a decision that spends credibility rather than alpha, and because the alternative would have destroyed 56 percent of the corpus on the strength of a document rather than a measurement. hypothesis: assumedPriorityFeeLamports of 200000 is the priority fee a BUILD_CUSTOM leg actually pays
motivation: the fee was never measured and could not be: priorityFeeLamports() multiplied the routers unit price by a null unit limit and returned zero for every Jupiter route because Jupiter never sends SetComputeUnitLimit
sample_source: live /swap/v2/build responses at four notionals plus a live SVM calibration and three settled mainnet transactions
sample_window: SOL to USDC routes at 0.01 0.02 0.05 and 0.1 SOL built within one minute
metric: charged priority fee in lamports derived from each routes own bytes
result: 3018 to 3564 lamports against an assumed 200000 - a 56x overstatement
action_taken: set assumedPriorityFeeLamports to 8000 as a documented fallback and made the byte-derived value the primary source
notes: The applied compute limit derives to exactly 1006000 on every observed route: 7 instructions of which 2 are builtin at 3000 units and 5 are BPF at 200000. That figure is corroborated three ways - a live SVM charged 6000 for two builtins and 9000 for three and clamped an explicit 2000000 to 1400000 all measured off the payer balance at one lamport per unit; a real Jupiter route logged consumed 183 of 1000499 compute units which is 1006000 less the early instructions; and three settled mainnet transactions reproduce their fees to the lamport. This is an availability correction and not an outcome-driven one: no return series was consulted. It moves costs DOWN which flatters the strategy,  so it is recorded with more care rather than less. 8000 is roughly 2.2x the dearest observed fee and covers a doubling of the routers unit price; it is a fallback only,  because the per-leg fee is computable from the bytes and a constant is still an assumption. Every economic number produced before this change carried a phantom 99 bps per leg and 198 bps per round trip at the 0.02 SOL size.

hypothesis: contextSlot is present on a BUILD_CUSTOM response and can be required before an observation is accepted

metric: fraction of observations where context_slot is populated
result: 0 of 22177 - Jupiter /swap/v2/build does not return it at all
action_taken: removed contextSlot from the hard refusal in missingBuildField and moved it into legIsConfirmatory as a blocker on confirmatory grading only
notes: This was caught by an end-to-end test rather than by the unit tests,  which passed: the unit fixtures supplied a contextSlot because the directive said the field existed. The first live build after the change came back MISSING_CONTEXT_SLOT,  and the corpus then showed the field has never once been populated. As written it would have refused 100 percent of builds and halted all collection while every unit test stayed green. That is the same defect already recorded as MT001 and MT002 and the invariant is explicit: absence of a provider field is a fact about the provider,  not about the token,  and never hard-vetoes. The field remains genuinely load-bearing - an offline replay needs a slot to stand at or lookup tables extended since will not resolve - so its absence blocks the row counting as evidence rather than blocking the row existing. No confirmatory window can open until a slot source is found.

hypothesis: the candidate sampler must spread across pools before deepening on any one
motivation: the first development window opened the SAME three mints on consecutive cycles; the sampler ordered by slot with no reference to what it had already sampled

A hundred paths across three pools is three outcomes with a hundred observations of them, and the 100-path threshold would have been met while supporting no claim about a population. The cap is 3 rather than 1 because the same pool at a different hour is a different market, so a repeat is informative but not independent.

hypothesis: the frozen 0.02 SOL notional is too large relative to the pools the sampler reaches
motivation: the entry impact bound was computed and DISCARDED (`void impact`) with hardcoded zeros written to every trajectory row; wiring it through revealed entries at 70-112% of pool quote reserve
sample_source: development window V1 candidates
metric: entry quote in as a fraction of effective quote reserve
result: 70.5% and 111.7% against a 0.5% small-impact bound; haircuts of 14110 and 22346 bps
action_taken: NONE YET - recorded, and the real bound is now stored per trajectory instead of a hardcoded zero. Neither the notional nor a minimum-depth filter has been changed.
notes: A round trip at 112% of a pool's quote reserve measures our own footprint rather than the venue, and any counterfactual exit built on it is dominated by self-impact. The fix is either a smaller notional or a minimum effective-quote-reserve admission gate, and BOTH are preregistered acts that must be decided before the next window rather than after seeing which produces better numbers. Deliberately left open.

hypothesis: the entry must be small relative to the pool it enters
motivation: the entry impact bound was computed and discarded; wiring it through showed the sampler was selecting drained pools where a 0.02 SOL entry is 6-170% of the quote reserve
sample_source: 29 readable confirmed-migration candidates, depth read live
metric: entry quote in as a fraction of effective quote reserve
result: 19 of 29 pools held 18-57 SOL (entry 0.1%); 10 were drained to 0.01-0.32 SOL (entry 6-170%)
action_taken: admission now refuses when the entry exceeds SMALL_IMPACT_BOUND of the effective quote reserve, and refuses on an unread reserve
notes: NOT a new threshold. SMALL_IMPACT_BOUND (0.5%) was already frozen in this repository for counterfactual validity and was being computed and discarded while the admission gate ignored depth entirely; this makes one threshold consistent with itself. Chosen on POOL DEPTH, before any policy outcome was examined, and it does not starve the study: 19 of 29 candidates qualify. Supersedes the open item MT039, which asked whether the notional was wrong - it is not, the candidate selection was.

hypothesis: the exploration arm must actually run, and its budget must survive a restart
motivation: allocate() existed, was tested, was pure, and no production caller invoked it, so 100% of the budget went to the ranking while pnpm exploration:status - an alias for cohort:status - reported on a different question
sample_source: the exploration entitlement ledger, empty at the time of the change
metric: fraction of opened trajectories drawn by the random arm
result: 0 of 187 - no trajectory had ever carried an arm, because the arm had never been invoked
action_taken: wired allocate() into the collector open path and made the entitlement a database ledger keyed by window and stratum
notes: NOT a threshold change. EXPLORATION_FRACTION stays at the frozen 25%; what changed is that the frozen fraction is now applied instead of being computed by nobody. The ledger is in the database because the collector is a daemon that restarts and an in-memory entitlement makes 25% mean "25% of whatever happened between crashes".

hypothesis: exploration entitlement must be earned by rows that exist, not by rows that were selected
motivation: the first live cycle selected eight candidates, the depth gate refused all eight, and the ledger still recorded granted 3 consumed 0 - so every cycle would add budget for rows that never existed
sample_source: one live collector cycle under the selection-based grant
metric: granted entitlement units versus trajectories opened
result: 6 units granted across two strata against 0 trajectories opened
action_taken: moved the grant after the open loop and keyed it on rows actually opened; deleted the 6 phantom units, none of which had been consumed
notes: Found by RUNNING the thing rather than by reading it. Deleting the phantom grants lost no history because consumed was zero on both rows; had anything been spent the script refuses rather than zeroing. Consequence, stated: the first window is now all exploitation, visibly, because a stratum earns its budget from the cycle before.

hypothesis: a signature listing whose newest slot is below the exit slot indicates an incomplete listing
motivation: the first live full-event-replay run refused a real pool with EVENT_LIST_INCOMPLETE
sample_source: one armed pool, 3Ydh3BiTFP4h, entry slot 439739457
metric: newest listed slot versus exit slot
result: newest listed slot 439484116, exit slot 439740409 - the pool had not traded in 255341 slots
action_taken: removed the forward-bound refusal; only an empty listing is refused now
notes: The hypothesis was WRONG and the run proved it. getSignaturesForAddress is queried newest-first with no cursor, so a newest slot below the exit is the observation that nothing traded, not evidence of a gap. The check was rejecting quiet pools - the one case where the replay is trivially exact. The backward bound (the listing must reach back past the entry) is unchanged and still refuses.

hypothesis: the reject panel must be prospective, so its horizons and metric are fixed before any row is admitted
motivation: reject:panel-v2 aliased trajectory-status.ts, which answers what the OPENED trajectories are doing - the opposite population - and the prospective panel did not exist at all
sample_source: reject_tracking, which records that a token was rejected but not the state it was rejected on
metric: rows carrying the snapshot the rejection was made on
result: 0 of 1191281 - the state was never stored, so every score would be computed against state fetched later
action_taken: added prospective_panels, prospective_samples and prospective_sample_marks; the rule is a literal in source frozen at 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z; admission refuses a row rejected before the rule, and marking refuses an undeclared horizon
notes: The 1191281 existing rows are NOT back-admitted. A panel cannot be made prospective after the fact, and merging them would be exactly the retrospective panel this replaces. Horizons mirror the trajectory mark offsets so both populations are observed on one schedule; the metric is an executable quote rather than a USD price, because 93% of a previous corpus had no route at all.

hypothesis: the mark grid must be able to express the exit-policy comparison it exists to make
motivation: the 8f73cef audit found no constructed path where FLOW_LIQUIDITY_DETERIORATION_V1 exits EARLIER than FIXED_15M_CONTROL at a different mark - and the cause turned out to be the grid, not the policy
sample_source: the mark offsets themselves, before any outcome existed under the current contract
sample_window: no window has opened under contract-d2b2bf4f5f83b0a1
metric: whether a deterioration detected before 15 minutes can be FILLED before 15 minutes
result: impossible on the 1/5/15/30/60 grid: the challenger needs two measured marks to see a drop, so the earliest trigger is 5m, and the first mark after 5m is 15m - the control's own horizon
action_taken: added 3m and 10m horizons, so a drop between 1m and 3m triggers at 3m and fills at 5m
notes: AVAILABILITY-driven, not outcome-driven: no outcome exists under this contract, and the change was forced by P9.2 requiring the challenger to fill at the first LATER valid mark rather than at the one that revealed the deterioration. Pricing it at the trigger books the exit at the one observation the strategy demonstrably could not have traded at. With the old grid the challenger could only ever differ by holding LONGER, and with heavy-tailed returns exiting early is the half of the hypothesis most worth testing. Cost: seven marks per trajectory instead of five.

hypothesis: the candidate queue must be able to reach candidates the gates would admit
motivation: the collector refused EVERY candidate on depth while eleven admissible pools sat untouched under the per-mint cap
sample_source: live effective quote reserves read for all 58 confirmed migrations at 2026-08-17T05:15Z
metric: pools with >= 4 SOL effective quote reserve, which is what a 0.02 SOL entry at the 0.5% bound requires
result: 38 of 58 deep enough; 11 of those still under the cap; deepest 184.7 SOL where the entry is 0.01% of the pool - and the collector refused everything it looked at, at 14.3% to 568.1%
action_taken: candidate ordering sinks a mint whose most recent risk-fact reading refused it for DEPTH; least-sampled-first is preserved within each group
notes: A STARVATION LOOP, not a threshold problem. Least-sampled-first is right, and combined with a gate that PERMANENTLY refuses part of the population it is self-defeating: a drained pool is refused on depth, so it is never sampled, so it stays least-sampled, so it returns to the head of the queue on the very next cycle, forever. The corpus shows both ends at once - one mint at 58 trajectories while eleven admissible pools sat untouched. Sinking rather than excluding, because a pool can recover and a mint that is shallow now is a legitimate candidate later; it just must not block the ones admissible today. NO GATE WAS WIDENED: the 0.5% depth bound, the per-mint cap and the notional are all unchanged.

hypothesis: the entity-adjusted concentration gate must compare a share of SUPPLY, because that is what its limit means
motivation: the first deep pool the repaired window ever saw was refused at 'entity-adjusted share 71.0% vs limit 50.0%' with every other gate passing, and the number was not a share of the token
sample_source: three live mints walked end to end (6zz4T7Vb7Q, 2XVHivUmgW, Eztcckaju2) plus the 11 corpus rows carrying a raw share
sample_window: one instant, before any trajectory opened under contract-cc437a9a9be4ba57
metric: the entity figure expressed as a share of supply, against the raw figure the same gate already accepts
result: the raw share across the corpus runs 11.4% to 47.2% of SUPPLY (mean 30.6%); the entity figure was coming out at 71.0%, 74.9%, 92.5% and 97.3% because concentration() reports over the holders it is handed, not over supply. Rebased: 20.68%, 19.42% and 36.22% of supply
action_taken: measureEntityTier scales the within-holders figure by the examined set's own share of supply, so the number reaching admitCandidate means what the limit means. The limit itself is unchanged at 50%
notes: NOT A WIDENING. concentration() is right to report over the holders it was handed - the number it exists to produce is the GAP between the entity and address readings, and both need one denominator. The defect was handing that figure to a gate whose other input (rawTopHolderShare = held/supply.amount) is a share of supply: two different quantities compared against limits written for one of them. Left uncorrected the entity gate refuses every candidate forever, which is not a strict gate, it is a broken instrument. The GAP survives the rebase and is the point: Eztcckaju2 reads 36.22% entity against 30.91% address, 19 addresses resolving to 16 entities with one funder behind four of them. Program-owned holders stay out of the entity numerator because they belong to no wallet cluster; the RAW tier counts them and both gates run.

hypothesis: the per-mint cap of 3 is enforced over SAMPLES, not over rows that mention a sample
motivation: a fresh window refused RESERVATION_CAP_REACHED on 24 of 25 candidates; the ordinal was reservations + historic trajectories + 1 and an OPENED reservation is already counted as a trajectory
sample_source: trajectory_reservations joined to development_trajectories over confirmed_migrations
metric: mints admissible under a cap of 3
result: 47 admissible before the correction, 124 after; example mint 6zz4T7Vb7Q6M scored ordinal 5 for 2 samples
action_taken: the cap VALUE is unchanged at 3; only the count was corrected so that a sample is counted once (S092)
independent_confirmation: not required - no outcome or return was consulted, and the change was made because candidates were unavailable rather than because results improved
notes: this is a defect repair rather than a threshold move, recorded here because it changes which candidates are admissible and CLAUDE.md requires that to be written down before it lands

hypothesis: MIGRATION_MICROSTRUCTURE_RISK_V1 removes catastrophic launch structures without removing right-tail winners
motivation: every smart-policy input at aaf6d6a was the literal null, so HARD_GATES_RANDOM was the only arm that could enter and the tournament had no economic content
sample_source: no Epitaxy outcome was consulted; the families come from MemeTrans (>40k migrated launches), SolRugDetector and Pump.fun graduation work, and the values come from protocol mechanics
sample_window: no window has opened under this policy
metric: eight decision-bearing conditions, each a catastrophe bound rather than a central tendency
result: creator net selling <= 0 lamports; entity concentration <= 0.60; largest first-buyer entity share <= 0.70; early buyer retention >= 0.20; late sell pressure <= 0.80; migration path entity dominance <= 0.70; mint behaviour safe; mechanics viable
action_taken: registered before the window opens; the policy decides on every trajectory and enters only where all eight hold
notes: REGISTERED BEFORE ANY OUTCOME EXISTS, which is what makes it availability-driven rather than alpha-spending. Every threshold is deliberately EXTREME rather than central - the survivor policy uses 0.35 for entity concentration and this uses 0.60 - because the job is to refuse the launch that is one wallet in a trench coat, not to prefer the tidiest token. Epitaxy's own window C had 2 of 13 paths positive with one ~+14m lamport winner carrying the total, so a filter tuned to raise the win rate would remove the paths that carry the strategy. A test asserts that a volatile-but-sound launch (late sell pressure 0.75, entity concentration 0.55, first-buyer share 0.65) still ENTERS; that assertion fails first if anyone tightens these to improve a summary statistic.

hypothesis: size is chosen from the pool's mechanics rather than fixed at an arbitrary research notional
motivation: the flat 0.02 SOL entry caused depth refusals where the proposed position was an absurd fraction of the pool, removing real market observations for a reason that had nothing to do with the market
sample_source: the size rule is evaluated from one coherent snapshot per candidate; no outcome or return is an input to it
sample_window: no window has opened under the dynamic rule
metric: the largest candidate size satisfying every frozen bound
result: candidate sizes 0.0025 / 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02 SOL; bounds unchanged at reserve share <= 50 bps, price impact <= 50 bps, bounded-counterfactual impact <= 10 bps, warm round-trip drag <= 400 bps
action_taken: the notional became a rule; every candidate size is evaluated and persisted with the condition that bound it
notes: NO SAFETY BOUND WAS WIDENED. Every limit is the one the fixed notional already had to clear; what changed is that the rule now asks what size fits this pool instead of whether the pool fits one number. 0.02 SOL is retained as the CEILING. An unmeasured bound refuses, so a size whose impact could not be computed is never chosen. chooseSize takes no return, no mark and no future state - the type signature is the guarantee, not the discipline.

hypothesis: two primary entry clocks (T0 and T120) rather than a grid over delays
motivation: the collector's only entry was at the first mechanically valid post-migration state, which buys with no post-migration confirmation at all
sample_source: no outcome was consulted; T120 was chosen from the observation requirement, not from a delay search
sample_window: no window has opened with a delayed arm
metric: paired T0-versus-T120 outcomes within the same mint
result: 120 seconds: long enough to observe post-migration buyer persistence, short relative to the 15-minute primary horizon, and pairable within a mint
action_taken: T0 and T120 are the only primary treatments; 30/60/180/300s are recorded as descriptive snapshots and are NOT entry treatments
notes: A grid over ten delays would spend the multiple-testing budget on a nearly continuous dimension where the winner of a ten-way search at this sample size is noise. Two clocks pair within a mint, which removes the token-selection variance that dominates everything else here. The descriptive offsets are explicitly barred from inference so they cannot become six delays by the back door; a test asserts T0 and T120 cannot share a decision-time snapshot, because reusing one is the obvious optimisation and would silently turn the delayed arm into a relabelling of the immediate one.

hypothesis: the six smart-policy signal inputs are computed from strictly pre-decision data
motivation: independentBuyerPersistence, nonMayhemNetQuoteInflowLamports, effectiveQuoteReserveTrend, executableExitCapacityTrend, continuationSlope and creatorNetSellingLamports were all the literal null at aaf6d6a
sample_source: definitions frozen before any outcome under them exists
sample_window: no window has opened with non-null signals
metric: non-null coverage per field, reported by pnpm policy:coverage
result: persistence window 60s; exit-capacity reference fraction 1.0 of the held position; continuation slope from LOG EXECUTABLE price normalised per second with the pre-existing vertical cap of 5
action_taken: signals are filled from the closed pre-migration curve at T0 and from confirmed post-migration flow at T120, with the SOURCE of every value recorded
notes: The T0/T120 asymmetry is deliberate and is the experiment: at T0 there is by construction no post-migration flow, so filling T0 from later flow would hand it information it could not have had and destroy the comparison. Every null carries a recorded reason, because a null nobody can explain is indistinguishable from a bug and six of them in a row was exactly that. Where Mayhem flow cannot be isolated the answer is null rather than ordinary net flow: an unseparated number answers a question nobody asked.
